newsitem.title: USA: Danish mother reunited with her baby in New York.
newsitem.headline: Danish mother reunited with her baby in New York.

text.p: A Danish actress was reunited on Wednesday with her baby, whom authorities had put in foster care for four days after the mother left her parked in a stroller outside a New York restaurant.
Attorneys for the mother said such a practice was common in Copenhagen, but officials questioned the wisdom of being so trusting in New York.

Authorities took 14-month-old Liv Sorensen from her Danish mother, Annette Sorensen, and American father, Exavier Wardlaw, on Saturday. The couple had left her outside an East Village restaurant while they were inside having a drink and watching her through the window, police said.
Passers-by said the baby was cold and crying and called police, they said.

The mother-and-child reunion took place at the Danish Seaman's Church in Brooklyn, according to local television. The church confirmed that the two will stay there until Sorensen's legal problems are resolved.
News programmes showed her bringing her daughter's brown stuffed dog to the meeting and later crying outside the church and kissing the child repeatedly.

The reunion, after days of legal wrangling, "went as smoothly as could be expected," Maggie Lear, a spokeswoman for the city's Administration of Children's Services, said. "They were happy to see each other," she added.
The parents face charges of endangering the welfare of a child and disorderly conduct.
"Leaving a child unattended on a city street for an hour in New York seems to me pretty inappropriate," Nicholas Scoppetta, head of the child agency, said earlier.
A similar incident "would never happen in Denmark," Michael Dyrby, an editor for Denmark's TV2 Denmark, told CNN.
"It happens all the time you have your child with you that you leave them outside a restaurant or outside of a shop," he said.
"In Denmark, it's very unusual that authorities interfere ... in family matters," he said. "We consider that the mother knows what's best for the child."
A New York Family Court judge late on Tuesday ordered the baby returned to her mother, but procedural issues took a day to resolve, authorities said.
Among other problems, plans for the mother and child to stay in the Danish Consulate had to be abandoned because of the need for social workers to visit, Scoppetta said.
Under the judge's order, another adult must always be present when the baby is with her mother.
David Kirsch, the father's attorney, said Sorensen had been in the United States less than 48 hours when her daughter was taken from her.
She and Wardlaw are due in Criminal Court on Monday, and she must return to Family Court after that for a hearing on custody of the child. Sorensen has already spent two days in jail.
